hypotheses.title: ABC35 extends lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Treatment with ABC35 extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The compound increases mean and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Small molecules can modulate conserved longevity pathways such as nutrient sensing and stress resistance. ABC35 may activate cellular maintenance mechanisms that slow aging in worms.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms exposed to ABC35 will show a statistically significant increase in mean and maximum lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Perform a lifespan assay with synchronized worms on ABC35-supplemented and control plates, scored blind, with three biological replicates and log-rank analysis of survival curves.

hypotheses.title: Ethosuximide extends lifespan via insulin/IGF-1 signaling inhibition
hypotheses.claim: Ethosuximide extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by inhibiting the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway. Reduced pathway activity mediates the longevity effect of the compound.
hypotheses.rationale: The insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway is a conserved regulator of aging, and its inhibition activates FOXO-dependent stress responses. Ethosuximide may act upstream to suppress this pathway and promote longevity.
hypotheses.prediction: Ethosuximide will extend lifespan in wild-type worms but will fail to further extend lifespan in long-lived insulin/IGF-1 signaling mutants.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare ethosuximide effects on lifespan in wild-type worms and in daf-2 and daf-16 mutants, measuring survival and DAF-16 nuclear localization.

hypotheses.title: Palmostatin B extends lifespan by reducing insulin-like signaling
hypotheses.claim: Palmostatin B extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by inhibiting protein depalmitoylation and reducing insulin-like signaling. Altered palmitoylation dynamics suppress insulin-like pathway output to promote longevity.
hypotheses.rationale: Protein palmitoylation regulates the membrane localization of insulin pathway components, and its inhibition can dampen pathway activity. Reduced insulin-like signaling is a conserved trigger of longevity programs.
hypotheses.prediction: Palmostatin B will extend lifespan in wild-type worms, reduce insulin-like signaling output, and fail to further extend lifespan in insulin-like signaling mutants.
hypotheses.experiment: Measure lifespan and insulin-like signaling reporters in wild-type and daf-2 or age-1 mutant worms treated with palmostatin B, comparing survival curves with log-rank analysis.
